q: my cold emails never get a reply, not even a no

why: Follow-up emails are free; effectively unlimited attempts

why: Written offer routed to multiple channels beats one gatekeeper

why: No candidate compares calling vs emailing as channels

q: best day and time to send cold outreach to contractors
why: Tuesday late-morning for email; Tuesday arrival for mail

why: No candidate addresses a stalled post-info-request lead

q: how do i follow up again without sounding desperate
why: Give value, not just repeated pitches; unlimited free follow-ups

why: Snail mail pitches outsell email pitches 20-40x

why: The list/audience matters more than the message

why: Engineer a paradigm change instead of announcing sales intent

why: No candidate makes this first-contact-ask distinction

why: No candidate addresses ghosting after a good first call

q: how long should a cold email be to a busy owner
why: No candidate sets cold-email length for a busy owner

q: i hate cold calling, is there a way around it
why: No candidate offers a real alternative to cold calling

q: how do i restart a conversation with a lead from six months ago
why: No candidate addresses reviving a dormant six-month lead

q: should i write my outreach in french or english here
why: Archive has zero coverage of French/English outreach choice

q: i get replies but they are all polite brush offs
why: No candidate addresses a pattern of polite brush-offs

q: i've rewritten this headline nine times and it still feels flat
why: Concrete headline formulas; flat headline often means no Big Idea

q: how do i open a sales letter when nobody knows who i am
why: 26 real openers; curiosity-fact opener skips needing credibility

q: my copy sounds like a corporate brochure, how do i fix that
why: Drop the polished corporate image; commit 'image suicide'

q: should this page be short or should i write out everything
why: Never too long, only too boring; length should fit audience intent

q: i'm staring at a blank doc, how do i start writing
why: Mechanical priming process to start; just write, don't wait

q: how do i tell if my own copy is any good
why: Read copy aloud; stumbling reveals rough, unpersuasive spots

q: my french version feels stiff next to the english one
why: Archive has zero coverage of French translation quality

q: what do i cut first when the letter runs too long
why: Cut 'that's, then self-referential 'I' clauses, first

q: how do i write a headline that isn't a boring feature list
why: Use a name, news, or a benefit promise, not a feature list

q: my copy is all about me and not about the reader
why: Hunt down and cut self-referential 'I', shift to 'you'

q: everything i write sounds like every other agency in town
why: Stop writing slogans; substantive long copy beats generic taglines

q: how do i make web design sound interesting instead of generic
why: Sales copywriting, not polished design, is what actually sells

q: should i use bullets or full paragraphs in a sales email
why: No candidate makes this bullets-vs-paragraphs call

q: i can't figure out what order to put my arguments in
why: Rank notes by importance, sequence them through AIDA

q: how many headlines should i write before i pick one
why: No candidate gives a concrete headline-count practice

q: the writing is fine but nothing in it makes anyone act
why: The offer, not the writing, is the heart of persuasion

q: how do i edit my own draft without killing what's good
why: Write fast and passionate first; tone down only after

q: should i write like i talk or clean it up first
why: Rehearse it like speech first in plain language, tweak later

q: how do i price a website project without pulling a number out of nowhere
why: No candidate covers service/project pricing methodology

q: prospects say the price is fine and then never sign
why: Trust behavior over stated words; people's mouths lie

q: should i put a money back guarantee on marketing work
why: Money-back guarantee is legal if honored; never guarantee results

q: what do i do when they say i need to think about it
why: No candidate addresses the 'need to think about it' stall

q: everyone says too expensive, is that the price or the offer
why: Price is psychological/relative; the offer usually is the real issue

q: should i sell packages or bill hourly for small local clients
why: No candidate compares package vs hourly billing

q: how do i add extras without making the whole thing look cheap
why: No candidate addresses bonus-stacking without cheapening the offer
